record.summary: Proposed directive that would have set common rules for non-contractual, fault-based civil claims for damage caused by AI systems. National courts could order providers or users of a high-risk AI system suspected of causing damage to disclose evidence, and would presume non-compliance with a duty of care where a defendant failed to do so. Courts would also presume a causal link between the defendant's fault and the AI system's output under set conditions; for providers of high-risk systems, fault meant breaching AI Act requirements on training data, transparency, human oversight, accuracy, robustness or cybersecurity. Both presumptions were rebuttable.
record.notes: Proposed on 28 September 2022 (COM(2022) 496 final, procedure 2022/0303(COD)). With the revision of the Product Liability Directive it formed a package covering different types of liability: this proposal national claims based on fault, the Product Liability Directive producers' no-fault liability for defective products. Article 5 would have required the Commission to review the directive and to evaluate whether no-fault liability rules and insurance cover are needed for certain AI systems. Annex IV of the Commission's 2025 work programme (COM(2025)45 final of 11 February 2025) listed it for withdrawal, giving the reason 'No foreseeable agreement' and adding that the Commission would assess whether another proposal should be tabled or another type of approach chosen. The Commission approved the withdrawal at its meeting of 16 July 2025, and the withdrawal was published in the Official Journal C series on 6 October 2025 (C/2025/5423); the European Parliament's procedure file records the proposal as withdrawn by the Commission on that date.

verification.note: Stored and read in this run: the EUR-Lex text of the proposal COM(2022) 496 (HTML of 17 Oct 2026, identical in text to that of 11 Oct 2026, and the PDF), which confirms the title, the date of 28 Sept 2022, the procedure number and the provisions in the summary; and the EUR-Lex notice C/2025/5423 'Withdrawal of Commission proposals' (OJ C, 6 Oct 2025), which lists COM(2022)496 final, 2022/0303 (COD) and says the Commission approved the withdrawals on 16 July 2025, with reasons in COM(2025)45 final (Annex IV). Also stored: the European Parliament's Legislative Observatory procedure file for 2022/0303(COD) (oeil.europarl.europa.eu, HTML and its PDF export), which gives the status 'Procedure lapsed or withdrawn' and the event '06/10/2025 Proposal withdrawn by Commission'; and the EUR-Lex text of the Commission Work Programme 2025 (COM(2025) 45 final), whose Annex IV, entry 32, gives the reason for the withdrawal. Version 1's claims from the EP Legislative Train were not used. The stored PDF of the 2019 political guidelines (document-1) is not about this proposal.

status.quote: COM(2022)496 final 2022/0303 (COD) Proposal for a DIRECTIVE OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL on adapting non-contractual civil liability rules to artificial intelligence (AI Liability)
The Commission has approved the withdrawal of those pending proposals during its 2533th meeting (16 July 2025).

summary.quote: the disclosure of evidence on high-risk artificial intelligence (AI) systems to enable a claimant to substantiate a non-contractual fault-based civil law claim for damages
a national court shall presume the defendant's non-compliance with a relevant duty of care
national courts shall presume, for the purposes of applying liability rules to a claim for damages, the causal link between the fault of the defendant and the output produced by the AI system
the AI system was not designed and developed in a way that allows for an effective oversight by natural persons during the period in which the AI system is in use
The defendant shall have the right to rebut the presumption laid down in paragraph 1.

notes.locator: Explanatory memorandum, consistency with other Union policies
notes.quote: These two policy initiatives are closely linked and form a package, as claims falling within their scope deal with different types of liability.

it should evaluate the appropriateness of no-fault liability rules for claims against the operators of certain AI systems, as long as not already covered by other Union liability rules, and the need for insurance coverage

judgment.status_reasoning: The European Parliament's procedure file for 2022/0303(COD) gives the status 'Procedure lapsed or withdrawn' and records '06/10/2025 Proposal withdrawn by Commission'; the OJ C notice C/2025/5423 of 6 Oct 2025 lists COM(2022)496 final among the withdrawn proposals, approved by the Commission on 16 July 2025. A withdrawn proposal keeps the status 'Revoked / withdrawn' and legal force 'Proposed'. The withdrawal is the latest event; nothing re-tables the proposal.
judgment.scope_reasoning: AI-specific EU legislative proposal on civil liability for AI, kept after withdrawal for context; in scope without a note.
